header: Structural Chemistry of Two-Dimensional Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides and Their Derivatives (26 points, 12%). Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides, or TMDs, generally have layered structures held together by van der Waals forces. Their symmetry and physical properties change substantially as the number of layers decreases.

subquestions.text_open:
Structural background: $WSe_2$ has a molybdenite-type hexagonal layered structure. The figure below is a projection along $a$; large spheres represent W and small spheres Se. One unit cell contains two layers along $c$.
5-1-2 Explain how W and Se occupy the hexagonal plane lattice in a projection along the c axis, and give the projected relationship within one unit cell.

text_images.description: A two-dimensional projection of a vertical rectangular unit cell outlined by thin black lines. Axes at the lower left show c vertically upward and b horizontally to the left. The figure contains two larger gray spheres and eight smaller green spheres joined by slender cylindrical bonds. An upper gray sphere lies inside the upper half of the cell near its right boundary and is connected to four green spheres at the upper-left, lower-left, upper-right, and lower-right positions. The two green spheres on the left lie within the cell, whereas the two on the right lie outside the right boundary. A lower gray sphere lies inside the lower half near the left boundary and is likewise connected to four green spheres at the upper-left, lower-left, upper-right, and lower-right positions. The two green spheres on the left lie outside the left boundary, whereas the two on the right lie within the cell. The two gray spheres are not directly connected; together they form two separate four-coordinate units offset vertically and oriented in opposite horizontal directions.

rubric: In the projection along c, W and Se occupy the A and B sites, respectively, of the hexagonal plane lattice. Only one set of W sites and one set of Se sites need be shown in a unit cell (2 points). If the A and B sites are correct but the C sites are also occupied incorrectly, award 1 point. Occluded atoms need not be shown repeatedly.

rubric_images.description: A two-dimensional projection of a parallelogram unit cell outlined by thin black lines. The figure contains two larger gray spheres and five smaller green spheres joined by slender cylindrical bonds. A gray sphere lies toward the left inside the cell, with a green sphere directly in front of it so that only the left and upper parts of the gray sphere remain visible. This central green sphere connects in three directions: to a green sphere directly above by an approximately vertical bond, to a green sphere outside the left boundary at the lower left by a diagonal bond, and to another gray sphere at the lower right. The right gray sphere lies toward the lower-right interior of the cell and, besides the central green sphere, connects to two more green spheres: one outside the right boundary at the upper right and one outside the lower boundary directly below. Overall, the two gray spheres are staggered left and right within the cell, while the five green spheres occupy the left-center, upper, outer-left, outer-right, and lower-outer positions, forming a connected structure across the parallelogram boundaries.
